project.name: WiiXLaunch_TotK
project.author: Mindstormman
project.description: WiiXLaunch host for Tears of the Kingdom 1.2.1

identity.//: As botw.json - read-only data, never .text. Switch only; there is no Wii U Tears of the Kingdom.
identity.//switch: 0xC00000 from the start of read-only data. TOTK's .rodata.1 runs module+0x36D9B4B..0x41A9F9B and the RO segment starts at module+0x2B1A000, so this sits 0x40455 inside it with several megabytes of margin either side. RANGE verified from the section table; the bytes there have not been read, unlike botw.json's two. If the first boot fingerprints and the number is stable across runs, it is fine - and Slice() bounds-checks it against the section either way, so a wrong offset reports `cannot fingerprint` rather than hashing whatever followed.

switch.//: system_resource_size and extra_service_access must match TOTK 1.2.1's own main.npdm - the game's memory init fails at boot if the size is 0, and exlaunch's generic service list omits four that TOTK grants itself.
switch.//load_point: exl_main is too early on this SDK. nn::fs has no allocator until nnSdk installs one during init, so MountSdCardForDebug calls through a null pointer and dies in nn::fs::fsa::Register. 'fs_ready' waits for the first time the GAME opens a file, which is a fact about the filesystem rather than a guess about which game function runs when - hooking nninitStartup by offset did nothing, because that address is a PLT thunk main uses for its own calls and nnSdk goes straight to the real definition.

wiiu.//: There is no Wii U Tears of the Kingdom. Nothing to build.

cemu.//: Cemu runs Wii U titles. Nothing to build.

//samples: The example mods under examples/ are the framework's own and two of them are BotW's - e_player needs botw.player, c_patch carries BotW addresses. The loader refuses them by name on this host, which is the mechanism working, but they do not belong in a TOTK install and shipping them means a deploy can overwrite the mods that do.
